auth.name: Name
auth.switchToSignIn: Already have an account? Sign in

setup.title: Create your household
setup.description: A household holds your accounts and everyone who shares them. You can add people later.
setup.baseCurrencyHint: Everything is consolidated into this. Changeable later, but never silently.

dashboard.netWorthHint: What you own, less what you owe. An internal transfer changes nothing.
dashboard.equityNote: Opening balance, excluded from net worth
dashboard.emptyBody: Record a first transaction and the numbers above start working.
dashboard.title: Overview

quickAdd.title: Move money
quickAdd.description: Between two of your accounts. Net worth will not change - that is the point.
quickAdd.amountHint: A comma works as a decimal point.
quickAdd.sameAccount: The two accounts must be different.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.description: Everything the household owns or owes. Balances come from the ledger.
accounts.newDescription: It starts at zero. Record a transaction to put something in it.
accounts.name: Name
accounts.equityNote: Created with the household. It is the counterpart of your first deposit, not something you own.
accounts.empty: No accounts in this group yet.
accounts.closeHint: An account has to be empty before it can be closed.
accounts.foreignExcluded: {count, plural, =1 {# account is} other {# accounts are}} not in these totals, because Altitude does not convert currencies yet: {names}. Your totals are in {base}.
accounts.currencyAside: Not {base}, so this account will sit outside your totals until Altitude converts currencies. An account's currency cannot be changed afterwards - you would open another one.
accounts.institutionHint: Who holds it. Naming a bank Altitude can read lets an import find this account later.

transactions.title: Transactions
transactions.description: Every movement, newest first. Nothing here is ever edited or deleted.
transactions.reverseHint: A ledger is corrected by adding the opposite, never by editing. Both entries stay.

import.title: Import
import.description: Read a file from your bank, see what it would add, then decide.
import.accountsHint: A statement covers several accounts. Say which of yours each one is, or let Altitude create them.
import.verdictDaysApart: {days, plural, =1 {# day apart} other {# days apart}}
import.applyToAlike: Do this to the {count, plural, =1 {other one} other {# others}}

answer.merge: Nothing is added, and this line will not be offered again.
answer.skip: Nothing is added, and the next file will ask about it again.

import.mergedCount: {count, plural, =1 {# line matched to what you already had} other {# lines matched to what you already had}}
import.notCheckedYet: Duplicates are checked once every account is chosen.
import.problems: Rows that could not be read
import.imported: {count, plural, =1 {# transaction imported} other {# transactions imported}}
import.nothingToImport: Nothing in that file could be read.
import.wrongShape: This does not look like a {name} export. Import it anyway?
import.counterpartFor: Where the money for "{description}" came from

account.statementAccount: The account this statement is about

import.openAll: Create the {count, plural, =1 {missing account} other {# missing accounts}}
import.opened: {count, plural, =0 {Everything was already there} =1 {# account created} other {# accounts created}}
import.counterpartSummary: {count, plural, =1 {# movement crosses} other {# movements cross}} the edge of your household, filed under {account}.
import.counterpartDialogTitle: Where each of these came from
import.counterpartDialogHint: These are the movements that cross the edge of your household. Most are what the summary says; change the ones that are not.
import.historyEmpty: Nothing has been imported into this household yet.
import.undoBody: Every transaction {filename} added will be cancelled by its opposite. Nothing is deleted: the import and the corrections both stay in the ledger, and you can import the file again afterwards.
import.rolledBack: {count, plural, =1 {# transaction reversed} other {# transactions reversed}}
import.mappingHint: Altitude found the separator, the header row and how the dates are written. What it cannot know is what each column means.
import.columnReferenceHint: The bank's own number for each line. With it, importing the same file twice adds nothing.
import.amountOneColumn: One column, negative for money out
import.currencyFileHint: Used for every row, since the file has no currency column.
import.dateOrderAsk: Which day is "{value}"? Nothing in this column settles it, because no value in it has a number above twelve first.
import.columnStatusHint: The column saying whether a line went through.
import.skipStatusesHint: A reverted or refused payment is a line in the file that never moved money. Tick the states that mean the line did not happen; anything unticked is imported.
import.skippedRows: {count, plural, =1 {# line was} other {# lines were}} left out, because {states} means the movement did not happen.
import.groupRequiredHint: Without these two, the file cannot be read at all.
import.groupExtras: What helps, if the file has it
import.groupExtrasHint: None of these is required. The reference is what makes importing the same file twice add nothing.
import.groupStatesHint: A statement lists more than movements.
import.mappingRemembered: Read with the description kept from {name}.
import.changeMapping: Change how this file is read

categories.title: Categories
categories.description: What your movements were for, decided by rules you write. Nothing is guessed, and every category can be traced to one rule.
categories.categoriesHint: Add the ones you actually use. A category with no rule is still a category you can file something under by hand.
categories.rulesHint: Read in order, lowest number first. The first rule that fits decides, so put the narrow ones above the broad ones.
categories.patternHint: A regular expression, read against a cleaned-up label: upper case, no accents, no dates, long numbers replaced by #. Case does not matter.
categories.patternInvalid: That expression could not be read. Check the brackets.
categories.ruleIncomplete: A rule needs a name, something to look for, and a category.
categories.applyHint: Over what is already in your ledger. Entries you categorised by hand are left alone.
categories.wouldChange: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing would change} =1 {# entry would change} other {# entries would change}}
categories.applied: {count, plural, =1 {# entry categorised} other {# entries categorised}}
categories.deleteCategoryHint: Deletes the rules that file into it. Transactions keep their history and lose the label.
